evidence: Receiving online DO2: minimum observed 8.64 mg/L at t≈24.6 h; latest 11.06 mg/L at t=51.8 h — all far above the 2 mg/L hard limit.

Receiving delayed P assays: 0.047 g/L (t=59 h), 0.038 (t=119), 1.067 (t=179), 2.945 (t=239 h) — healthy product trajectory matching the source batches (e.g. source-2: 0.031, 0.0, 1.077, 3.017 at the same times).

Physical forward model (nominal, source-calibrated, transfer multiplier ≈1.036): reduce_feed predicts product mass 595.5 kg, post-decision min DO 9.27 mg/L, below_limit_h = 0, oxygen_deficit = 0; sensitivity: 5/5 feasible members, mass 590.1–602.0 kg, min DO 8.09–10.19 mg/L.
Model comparison of alternatives: keep/increase_air ≈576.3 kg, combined ≈595.5 kg with identical mass to reduce_feed but unnecessary air increase; stop = zero counted production.
All receiving DO2 observations and the last assay (t=239 h) are available at decision time 52.0 h; no extra assay was needed.
submission.rationale: Receiving batch observations show a normal, healthy process: online DO2 never fell below ~8.6 mg/L (latest 11.06 mg/L at 51.8 h), and delayed product assays track the source batches closely (P = 2.94 g/L at 239 h, on a rising trajectory). The source-calibrated physical forward model predicts every non-stop action is feasible with zero hours below the 2 mg/L DO limit and predicted minima of 8.3–9.6 mg/L; all sensitivity members are feasible for reduce_feed (min DO 8.09–10.19 mg/L), so this is not a case where feasibility depends on a favorable uncalibrated member. Among feasible plans, reduce_feed retains the most product mass (595.5 kg vs 576.3 kg for keep, +3.3%) because the milder feed rate raises terminal concentration while slightly reducing volume; it also increases the predicted DO margin (min 9.27 vs 8.30 mg/L under keep). combined gives the same predicted mass as reduce_feed without benefit, increase_air gives no mass benefit over keep, strong_feed_reduction is a larger deviation than evidence warrants, and stop would count zero production. Therefore the mild, bounded reduce_feed (feed × 0.8, air unchanged) is the recommended reviewable intervention.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated, not validated on this hidden receiving realization; the source-to-receiving transfer multiplier (≈1.036) and change-time estimate (t≈44 h) are model inferences. The mass advantage of reduce_feed over keep (~19 kg, ~3%) is within plausible model mismatch, and sensitivity members are not calibrated probabilities — but since all actions are feasible with very large DO margins (>8 mg/L vs the 2 mg/L limit) and all sensitivity members for reduce_feed remain feasible, the hard DO constraint is robustly respected. If the receiving process deviates from the source behavior (e.g., a sharper DO sag after the model's estimated change point), online DO monitoring should be continued and the action revisited; the recommendation is a simulation output, not physical approval.
